title: How Morgan Stanley's 'mad scientist' became the top Wall Street analyst on the space industry
summary: Adam Jonas, Morgan Stanley's auto analyst, has become the firm's leading expert on the space industry, a shift driven by his interest in Elon Musk's ventures. Initially met with skepticism, Jonas and his team have built a comprehensive research effort on space, anticipating significant growth, akin to the self-driving car market. He believes catalysts like a Chinese lunar mission or a major tech company's satellite launch could rapidly accelerate market appreciation for space investments.

title: Apple iPhone and McDonald’s fast food have the same problem
summary: Apple Inc. and fast-food chains like McDonald's are facing a similar "demand problem" despite healthy sales figures. Both businesses are relying on higher prices or increased average checks to offset declining customer traffic or flat sales volumes, which the article argues is an unsustainable strategy given market saturation and economic cracks. The article suggests innovative tactics like embracing delivery for restaurants and aggressive marketing of add-on services for Apple to address these challenges.

title: UPS, FedEx shares fall into bear market as Morgan Stanley sees rising competition from 'Amazon Air'
summary: Shares of FedEx and UPS entered a bear market after Morgan Stanley warned about increasing competition from "Amazon Air." The firm believes Amazon Air poses a significant risk to the revenue of both delivery companies, estimating a potential 2% revenue loss this year, accelerating to over 10% by 2025. Morgan Stanley also noted substantial cost savings for Amazon by handling express shipping internally, leading to lowered price targets for UPS and FedEx.

title: Walmart’s newest team members are a fleet of robot janitors
summary: Walmart is deploying 360 autonomous floor-scrubbing robots to select stores nationwide by the end of January, partnering with Brain Corp for the AI technology. This initiative expands Walmart's existing use of automation, which includes shelf-scanning robots, to free employees from mundane tasks for customer service. The move highlights a broader retail trend towards automation, though experts warn of potential job displacement in labor-intensive roles.

title: The Children’s Place shifts to omnichannel, digital to reach millennial moms
summary: The Children's Place reported strong Q3 2018 results with net sales up 6.6% and digital sales rising 38%, now accounting for 29% of net sales. The retailer is on track to close 300 stores by 2020 and is focusing on omnichannel and digital strategies to attract and retain "millennial moms." The company is also reducing its reliance on China for sourcing, making it less vulnerable to tariffs.

title: Walmart introduces Dotcom Store service for online orders
summary: Walmart has launched its new Dotcom Store service, enabling store associates to place online orders for customers using handheld devices. This service allows customers to access a wider assortment of products available on Walmart.com from physical stores and pay using various methods. Walmart plans to integrate marketplace items into the app in the near future.

title: Walgreens Expands Prescription Delivery Program Nationwide
summary: Walgreensannounced the nationwide expansion of its prescription delivery program in partnership with FedEx, offering next-day delivery for $4.99 and same-day delivery in select cities. This move follows rival CVS Health's similar expansion and is a response to increasing online competition from companies like Amazon, which has acquired PillPack. Retailers are enhancing customer services to mitigate the impact of online retailers on drugstore sales.

title: Walmart acquires Art.com to boost online home decor business
summary: Walmart Inc. announced its acquisition of online retailer Art.com for an undisclosed amount to strengthen its home decor business and online presence. This move is part of Walmart's broader strategy to attract millennial customers and compete with rivals like Amazon, following several other e-commerce acquisitions. Art.com will operate as a standalone business, with its products eventually integrated into Walmart's online offerings.

title: Walgreens, FedEx team up on next-day prescription drug deliveries
summary: Walgreens and FedEx have launched a nationwide next-day delivery service for prescription drugs, leveraging FedEx's air and ground networks. Walgreens is also piloting a same-day delivery program in select cities. This move follows similar initiatives by rivals and comes amidst increased interest in pharmaceutical delivery, notably from Amazon.

title: Taking aim at Intel, Qualcomm launches chip for business PCs
summary: Qualcomm has launched a new series of chips, the Snapdragon 8cx, specifically designed for business PCs to directly compete with Intel. These new chips will support Windows 10 Enterprise, addressing a limitation of previous Qualcomm chips that only supported consumer versions of Windows. This move intensifies Qualcomm's competition with Intel, which has historically dominated the PC chip market and is also being challenged in the data center business.

title: Walmart turns to robots and apps in stores
summary: Walmart is implementing new technologies like robotic floor scrubbers and a "Dotcom Store" app to improve efficiency and customer experience in its physical stores. These initiatives aim to reduce costs, free up employees for other tasks, and offer more product options to customers, enabling Walmart to better compete with online retailers like Amazon. The company is actively testing various robots for tasks such as inventory management and grocery pickup, while also addressing potential concerns about job displacement.

title: Janus Henderson: Tech market sell-off - the bigger picture
summary: Alison Porter, Richard Clode, and Graeme Clark from Janus Henderson’s Global Technology Team discuss the recent tech market sell-off, attributing it to a combination of factors including rising bond yields, trade war concerns, and inventory correction in semiconductors. They highlight that despite the volatility, the long-term secular drivers for the technology sector remain strong, and valuations are becoming more attractive. The team emphasizes their valuation-disciplined investment style and focus on quality companies benefiting from powerful secular themes.

title: DR Horton, KB Homes: How Big Production Builders Deploy Smart-Home Technology Today
summary: Major home builders DR Horton and KB Home are integrating smart-home technology into their new constructions, recognizing the evolving expectations of homebuyers, especially Millennials. They emphasize the importance of "white-glove" service to assist customers with setup and understanding of these systems to ensure satisfaction. Both companies are now including base packages of smart devices in all their homes, prioritizing user-friendly platforms that integrate various devices and foregoing voice assistant-only systems due to privacy concerns.

title: Kroger buys pharmacy records from 42 Shopko stores
summary: Kroger has announced its acquisition of pharmacy records from 42 Shopko locations, a move that follows Shopko's decision to close 39 stores. This strategic purchase allows Kroger to expand its pharmacy presence and tap into an established customer network, especially in states like Wisconsin, Utah, and Montana. The deal underscores Kroger's commitment to investing in the pharmacy space and offering greater convenience to customers.

title: Governor: Norfolk Southern moving headquarters to Atlanta
summary: Norfolk Southern Corp. is relocating its headquarters from Norfolk, Virginia, to Atlanta, bringing 850 jobs and over $500 million in economic investment to Georgia. Governor Nathan Deal announced this move, highlighting Atlanta's appeal as a transportation and innovation hub. This decision reflects a broader trend of companies moving to major cities for deeper talent pools and better amenities, though it represents a psychological rather than a significant economic loss for Norfolk.

title: IAS Taps Ex-Yahoo Sales Boss Lisa Utzschneider as CEO of Ad-Verification Firm
summary: Integral Ad Science (IAS), a digital ad verification company, has appointed Lisa Utzschneider, former Yahoo chief revenue officer, as its new CEO and board member, effective January 7, 2019. She replaces Scott Knoll, who moves to an advisory role. Utzschneider's focus will be on global expansion and new ad formats following Vista Equity Partners' majority stake acquisition in IAS.

title: Postmates' Quest to Build the Delivery Robot of the Future
summary: Postmates has been secretly developing its own delivery robot, Serve, for the past two years, aiming to revolutionize last-mile deliveries. Serve, a child-sized cart with a friendly design, is intended to economize human worker routes by handling walking-distance deliveries that currently involve cars. The company faces challenges in public perception and integration into public spaces but hopes its anthropomorphic design will foster acceptance and redefine delivery logistics.

title: Info Junkie: Chandler Hatch
summary: This article features Chandler Hatch, a Sales Manager at Untappd, detailing his reliance on technology for both his professional and personal life. He shares his preferred publications, podcasts, TV shows, books, and social media recommendations, highlighting his engagement with technology, business, and craft beer culture.

title: Tricia Griffith
summary: This article highlights Progressive CEO Tricia Griffith's recognition as Fortune magazine's 2018 Businessperson of the Year, detailing the company's significant financial growth under her leadership, including a nearly 50% stock increase and profits more than doubling in the previous year. It also touches on Progressive's efforts in diversity and inclusion, with two women occupying top leadership roles and pay equity analysis results. The company's future growth strategy, including a new 40-person team and involvement in blockchain technology, is also discussed.

title: Costco buys Katy land that Hines had big plans for
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has purchased a 150-acre parcel in Katy, Texas, from Hines, which had initially planned to develop a 2.1-million-square-foot business park on the site. This acquisition solidifies the far west Houston region as a significant hub for distribution centers, with Costco planning to build a large-format distribution center. Hines, having sold the land for an attractive offer, now seeks other development opportunities in the Katy market due to its strategic logistics location.

title: Amazon Thrives on FedEx Delivery Model, but Driver Pay Challenges Persist
summary: Amazon is replicating the FedEx delivery model by recruiting independent contractors to handle last-mile deliveries, offering entrepreneurial opportunities despite potential challenges with driver pay and legal issues. This strategy helps Amazon meet surging demand and manage shipping costs but faces hurdles in attracting and retaining drivers in a tight labor market, potentially leading to lawsuits over worker classification. The article highlights how this approach allows Amazon to expand its delivery network rapidly, leveraging contractors to absorb the costs and complexities of hiring and managing a large driver workforce.

title: Global manufacturer eyes NKY for new location, hundreds of jobs
summary: A global manufacturer is exploring the possibility of opening a new facility in Northern Kentucky, a move that would create hundreds of new jobs in the region. Jabil, headquartered in St. Petersburg, is the company reportedly looking at this expansion. This potential development follows other recent large-scale investment announcements in the area.

title: No humans required: Kroger’s driverless delivery pilot enters next phase
summary: Kroger is expanding its driverless delivery pilot with Nuro, introducing Nuro's R1 vehicle which operates without a driver and is optimized for grocery transport. This initiative aims to enhance efficiency in online order fulfillment and compete with other major retailers in the e-commerce grocery market, despite ongoing questions about scalability and regulatory environments. The R1, designed to carry up to 20 grocery bags, operates on public roads but has limitations regarding speed, weather, and service areas.

title: Grocery delivery, with no human drivers, underway for King Soopers parent company Kroger
summary: Kroger and Nuro have launched a driverless grocery delivery service in Scottsdale, Arizona, using unmanned R1 vehicles. This initiative marks a significant step towards lowering delivery costs and advancing self-driving technology on public roads, despite current limitations and challenges. The service operates within a one-mile radius of a Fry's Food grocery store and is designed to prioritize safety.

title: Advertising: Why billboards and outdoor ads are booming in a smartphone age
summary: Despite the rise of digital advertising and smartphone addiction, billboards and outdoor ads are experiencing a resurgence. Major tech companies like Netflix, Apple, Google, and Amazon are investing heavily in out-of-home advertising, which offers relevance and bypasses ad-blocking software. The integration of technology, data, and programmatic buying is making these traditional ad formats more interactive, targeted, and effective in capturing consumer attention.

title: PW Notables of the Year: Randall White
summary: Randall White, Chairman, CEO, and president of Educational Development Corp. (EDC), dramatically grew the company's sales from $32.5 million in fiscal 2015 to $112 million in fiscal 2018. This growth was driven by his decision to stop selling to Amazon and to shift the company's direct selling efforts to online platforms, particularly Facebook. Despite significant operational challenges in 2016 due to rapid expansion, EDC implemented successful overhauls, leading to substantial earnings growth.

title: Accredo parent and Cigna finalize $54B merger
summary: Cigna has finalized its $54 billion acquisition of Express Scripts after receiving final regulatory approval. Although the combined company's headquarters will be in Connecticut, Express Scripts' headquarters is expected to remain in St. Louis. The deal brings together Accredo's parent company with Cigna.

title: Did you know Bubble Wrap was invented right here in Hawthorne?
summary: This article details the invention of Bubble Wrap in Hawthorne, NJ, by Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes in 1957. Initially intended as 3D wallpaper, it transformed into a packaging solution when IBM became its first major customer. The company, Sealed Air Corp., has since grown into a multi-billion-dollar enterprise, significantly boosted by the rise of e-commerce.

title: Pedialyte Is Embracing Its Reputation as a Hangover Treatment With a Sparkling Drink for Adults
summary: Pedialyte has launched a new product, Sparkling Rush, specifically targeting adults for hangover relief, playing into its long-standing off-label use. The new product is a fruit-flavored electrolyte powder designed to be mixed with water, providing a medical-grade hydration solution with twice the electrolytes and half the sugar of leading sports drinks. While not a cure for hangovers, it aims to alleviate symptoms by rehydrating and replacing electrolytes.

title: 5 Biopharma Trends to Watch in 2019
summary: This article forecasts five key biopharma trends for 2019, including the advancement of cancer immunotherapies beyond CAR-T cells, a continued rise in M&A driven by specialization and disruptive deals, the increasing integration of digital therapeutics, significant growth in cell and gene therapy investments, and the impact of Wall Street volatility on biopharma investments with a focus on China and the UK. Despite market declines, optimism for targeted acquisitions and new technologies remains high.
